summary: Horidor keeps its moot and its cairn roads: shield of the Northern Accord or a crown of its own, herds and passes, and a place beside Fandanar when the south burns.

chiefs_of_the_cairns.name: Chiefs of the Cairns
chiefs_of_the_cairns.desc: Every glen has its chief and every chief a cairn, and the moot is where the cairns are counted. Horidor is slow to decide and very slow to be moved.

highland_moot_united.name: One Moot, One Voice
highland_moot_united.desc: The chiefs still quarrel, but they quarrel inside the moot and leave it speaking as one. Envoys from abroad have learned to ask for the moot, not for any single chief.

accord_shield.name: Shield of the Accord
accord_shield.desc: Horidor stands in the Northern Accord and its borders are watched by friends. The cost is a share of every decision, and the benefit is a shield on the south and east.

two_banners_raised.name: Two Banners, One March
two_banners_raised.desc: The banner of the cairns and the banner of the Winter Crown are carried side by side. The columns drill together and learn each other's horn-calls.

own_hearth.name: Our Own Hearth
own_hearth.desc: Horidor warms itself at its own fire and asks no crown for leave. The chiefs are proud of it, and the cold has made them proud of little else.

wool_and_hide_trade.name: Wool and Hide
wool_and_hide_trade.desc: Fleeces and cured hides go down the cairn roads in long strings of wagons and come back as grain and salt. A well-clothed host does not fear the high winter.

pass_scouts.name: High-Pass Scouts
pass_scouts.desc: Scouts who have walked every pass since boyhood read the weather in the colour of the ridge. They are seldom surprised, and never twice.

highland_host.name: The Highland Host
highland_host.desc: The clan levies march under one banner, in step to the pipes of the moot. A highland host strikes hard on the first morning, when its blood is up.

valley_markets.name: Markets for the Valleys
valley_markets.desc: The independent valleys come to Horidor to sell, and Horidor opens its gates to buy. Goodwill grows where bargains are fair.

beside_fandanar.name: Beside Fandanar
beside_fandanar.desc: Horidor has chosen the Winter Crown's side in the war of the south, without marching beyond its own passes. The highlands hold, and the moot is easy in its conscience.

chiefs_grumble.title: The Chiefs Grumble
chiefs_grumble.desc: At the autumn moot, the oldest chiefs rise one by one to say that Fandanar has been speaking for the highlands again. Ollon waits until the last has finished, and then waits a little longer.

focuses.name: The Highland Moot
focuses.desc: Under the open sky, on a plateau ringed with cairns, the chiefs of Horidor meet to hear Chieftain Ollon and to say what he does not wish to hear. Nothing is decided that the moot has not heard.

focuses.name: Voices of the Cairns
focuses.desc: Each cairn is a name, and each name a family that has a voice in the moot. The old stones are set in order and the oldest voices are heard first.

focuses.name: Ollon's Hearth
focuses.desc: Ollon keeps a long hearth in the highland hall, and Old Tarvo, the Keeper of the Cairns, sits at its head. He remembers every oath ever sworn in Horidor and the name of every man who broke one.

focuses.name: The Chiefs Grumble
focuses.desc: Some chiefs say that Fandanar speaks for the highlands abroad without being asked. Ollon lets the grumbling be heard, for a grievance aired at the moot is a grievance half mended.

focuses.name: One Moot, One Voice
focuses.desc: At the autumn gathering the chiefs bind themselves to speak abroad with one voice, decided in the moot. It is the first time in a lifetime that every cairn has agreed on anything.

focuses.name: The Accord Question
focuses.desc: Horidor stands with Coldor in the Northern Accord, and the moot asks again what the Accord is: a league of equals, or a crown wearing a cloak. Envoys ride to every cairn with the question.

focuses.name: Shield of the Accord
focuses.desc: Ollon speaks for the shield. An Accord of equals keeps the passes safe and the herds fat, and Fandanar has never yet asked a highland chief to bend.

focuses.name: The Highland Crown
focuses.desc: Others say that Horidor was a kingdom before the Accord was a word, and that a kingdom keeps its own banner. The chiefs who say so are loud, and their cairns are old.

focuses.name: Highland Envoys
focuses.desc: Highland envoys sit in the Winter Crown's councils as equals, and say so. They carry back what they hear, and the moot weighs it before it acts.

focuses.name: The Accord's War Council
focuses.desc: The Accord's captains meet at Fandanar over a table of carved ridges, and Horidor's chiefs show the passes by name. When they ride home, both sides know the other's drill.

focuses.name: Two Banners, One March
focuses.desc: The highland host and the Winter Crown's companies drill on the same field, behind the same horn. A column that has marched beside its ally does not break when the ally is at its flank.

focuses.name: Our Own Hearth
focuses.desc: The moot hangs the highland banner above Ollon's hearth and swears to keep it there. No friend is turned away, and none is let sit in the high seat.

focuses.name: King of the Cairns
focuses.desc: A heap of stones is raised at the moot-ground, taller than any cairn, and the chiefs name it the King's Cairn. Whoever sits beside it is more than a chieftain.

focuses.name: The Cairn Crown
focuses.desc: Ollon is crowned beside the stones with a circlet of beaten iron, and the chiefs cry him king of the cairns. The Winter Crown hears of it, and does not smile.

effects.tooltip: Chieftain Ollon takes the title King of the Cairns.

focuses.name: Herds of the High Pastures
focuses.desc: Shaggy cattle and mountain sheep graze the high pastures from thaw to first frost, and the herd-wives know every beast by its voice. The wool, hide and cheese of Horidor go down the roads to the markets.

focuses.name: The Cairn Roads
focuses.desc: The old cairn roads, marked at every rise by a heap of stones, are widened and drained. A wagon that once took ten days to cross the passes takes six.

focuses.name: Wool and Hide
focuses.desc: Wool is carded in the glens and hide is tanned beside the rivers. Horidor's cloaks are warm enough to be sold as far south as the Windwaith harbours.

focuses.name: Granite and Iron
focuses.desc: The high cliffs yield granite for walls and the deep seams yield iron for blades. The moot allots the quarries by lot, so that no cairn grows richer than its neighbour.

focuses.name: Highland Stores
focuses.desc: Cold stone cellars are dug into the hillsides and filled with barley, cheese and salted mutton. When the winters come hard, Horidor feeds its own and has something to spare.

focuses.name: The Clan Levies
focuses.desc: When the horn sounds from the moot-ground, every glen sends its quota of spearmen. They bring their own blankets and bread, and they bring their cousins.

focuses.name: Cairn Wardens
focuses.desc: Each cairn names a warden to guard the passes under it, armed from the cairn's own stores. Better spears are forged for them, and they carry them with pride.

focuses.name: High-Pass Scouts
focuses.desc: Maela Highcairn teaches the scouts who watch the passes, and teaches them to read the snow like a page. A column that cannot be seen cannot be struck.

focuses.name: The Highland Host
focuses.desc: Once each summer the levies are drawn together in the great glen and shown how to move as a single host. When the pipes begin, the glens stop being a hundred bands and become an army.

focuses.name: Hill Forts
focuses.desc: Stone forts rise at the heads of the passes, each with a spring inside its walls. A fort on a high pass can be held by a handful against a host.

focuses.name: The Independent Valleys
focuses.desc: Below the highland passes lie valleys that bow to no crown, and Horidor's herdsmen have traded with them for longer than the Accord has had a name. The moot sends gifts and good words down the roads.

focuses.name: A Watch on Isengard
focuses.desc: To the south the iron hall of Isengard glowers at Fandanar, and the highland chiefs would rather watch it than fight it. Forts rise on the southern ridges, with horns at the ready.

focuses.name: Markets for the Valleys
focuses.desc: Horidor builds a market at the foot of each great pass, free of toll for a season. The valley folk come to sell cheese and stay to hear the moot's news.

focuses.name: A Seat at the Moot Fire
focuses.desc: A valley elder is given a seat at the moot's fire, to listen though not to vote. It costs Horidor nothing, and it makes friends of neighbours who would otherwise be strangers.

focuses.name: When the South Burns
focuses.desc: Smoke has risen in the south, and the great crowns are at war. The moot is called to the high ground, and Ollon asks what Horidor owes to a world beyond its passes.

focuses.name: Stand with Fandanar
focuses.desc: Horidor stands beside the Winter Crown, in the passes and at the moot, and says so openly. The highlanders will not march south, but no foe will pass them northward.

focuses.name: Ride with the White Companies
focuses.desc: If the White Companies ride south, some highland chiefs mean to ride with them. They have heard what the dark is doing, and they will not let it be said that Horidor stayed by its fire.

focuses.name: Highlanders Beside the Heir
focuses.desc: The highland spears go south to stand beside the host of the returned heir. They carry the banners of the cairns and march in step to a tune their grandfathers sang.
